# Source Sans Pro regular family and Black exact-face controls

Original eight-style DOCX generated by tools/source_sans_family_fixture.py.
Each sentence ends with an independently authored blue marker to measure its
advance in the reference application's PDF. Both regular and Black names cover plain, bold, italic
and bold-italic. The reference application exported native.pdf; source_sans_family_reference.py
records image origins and hashes. record_source_sans_family_ink.py separately
records 384-dpi native ink, using baseline-relative crops.

Current browser advances match all eight native markers within 0.006 pt.
All eight native ink ratios are within 2.34% (test limit 5%). The complete
native/browser page pair was visually inspected. Editing/export/reopen and
exact undo retain stored font names and unrelated package parts.

The reference application's embedded fonts identify Roman 2.021 / Italic 1.076. Reviewed Adobe
Regular/Bold/Black/BlackIt binaries are 2.045/1.095; regular-family It/BoldIt
are unmodified 1.075 to preserve the native advances. The later 1.095 regular
italic had a measured +0.900 pt sample-sentence advance difference. No spacing
adjustment or modified font binary is used. Provenance, corresponding editable
sources, licenses and all binary hashes are in public/fonts/PROVENANCE.md.

The reference application adds synthetic bold to the Black face even though its outlines are already
heavy. A family explicitly registered only at normal CSS weight now receives
synthetic paint when browser ink probing finds no bold effect. Native Arial
Bold/Arial Black and families with a real bundled bold companion stay unchanged.
The older Franklin Gothic Demi native-font gap remains an expected failure in
its own suite; this is not a claim that all installed-face synthesis is solved.
